reasons: Fixed figures and names are shown in place of values calculated from the case, so the dashboard can present made-up results as real.
The reset action is tied to demo behavior and is not guarded in this file.

terms.meaning: A historical land ownership record used in some Indian states.
A current land record that lists land holders and areas.
A small space in the browser that keeps data after the page is closed.
A short message that appears briefly on screen and then fades away.
A section that opens and closes when the user clicks its heading.
A dial-style graphic that shows where a value sits on a scale.
A React tool that lets a component remember values or run code when it appears.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the dashboard
sections.what: Brings in the tools, components, language labels, and data types the dashboard needs.
sections.why: Needed to draw the dashboard, read the language choice, and move between pages.

sections.name: CaseDashboardContent (part 1)
sections.title: Review marks and accordion state
sections.what: Remembers which differences are marked reviewed and which sections are open. Each change is saved in browser storage and shows a short message.
sections.why: Lets the user return to the dashboard and see the same review progress in this browser.
sections.watch_out: Review marks are stored only in this browser, so other users or devices do not see them.

sections.name: CaseDashboardContent (part 2)
sections.title: Reset and page helpers
sections.what: Handles the reset button by calling the demo reset endpoint and clearing review marks. It also provides a helper that scrolls to a section and calculates how many differences remain.
sections.why: Lets a demo be restarted from the screen and guides the user to the differences to review.
sections.watch_out: The reset endpoint is meant for demo cases. Its effect on a real case is not visible here.

sections.name: CaseDashboardContent (part 3)
sections.title: Labels and text for the dashboard
sections.what: Holds English and Hindi labels for the difference cards and buttons. Also builds the sentence that says how many differences are left.
sections.why: Keeps the text in one place so both languages stay consistent.
sections.watch_out: The step count is set to only 3 or 4 steps, so it does not follow the real number of checks.

sections.name: CaseDashboardContent (part 4)
sections.title: Header and area gap tile
sections.what: Shows the case name, village, khata, and khesra at the top, and an area gap tile with a fixed 15 percent figure and a scale bar.
sections.why: Gives the user the headline facts first.
sections.watch_out: The 15 percent figure and the position of the marker on the bar are fixed and do not update from the case.

sections.name: CaseDashboardContent (part 5)
sections.title: Area and name review tasks
sections.what: Shows two clickable task buttons, one for the area difference and one for the name difference, each with a done or to-do pill. Clicking scrolls to the differences section and opens that item.
sections.why: Lets the user jump straight to each difference that needs review and see whether it is done.
sections.watch_out: Both buttons share the same scroll target and update the open-differences state, so changes there affect both.

sections.name: CaseDashboardContent (part 6)
sections.title: Progress count and review tasks
sections.what: Shows the step count out of five and two task buttons, one for area and one for holder name. Each button opens the matching difference card.
sections.why: Lets the user jump straight to the next thing to review.
sections.watch_out: The status pill text switches with the saved review marks, so a mismatch between saved marks and the visible count is possible after a manual edit.

sections.name: CaseDashboardContent (part 7)
sections.title: Holders gauge
sections.what: Shows a dial with the number of holders and a text line about names matching in one of two records. The figures are fixed.
sections.why: Gives a quick visual of holder name agreement.
sections.watch_out: The dial needle position and the count of 1 are fixed in the code.

sections.name: CaseDashboardContent (part 8)
sections.title: Area gauge
sections.what: Shows a dial for the survey area and a legend with three area figures. The values are fixed.
sections.why: Lets the user compare the historical, survey, and computed areas at a glance.
sections.watch_out: All area values are fixed, so the gauge will not match a different parcel.

sections.name: CaseDashboardContent (part 9)
sections.title: Field match bars
sections.what: Shows a summary of how many of four checks agree, with bar charts for area, holder, khata, and khesra. The bars and the 2 of 4 count are fixed.
sections.why: Gives a fast view of where records agree or differ.
sections.watch_out: Bar heights and counts are fixed in the code, so they will not reflect a real comparison.

sections.name: CaseDashboardContent (part 10)
sections.title: Map tile and area difference card
sections.what: Shows the map tile and the first difference card. The card lets the user open the area details, see two area figures side by side, and mark the item reviewed.
sections.why: Puts the area question next to its evidence so the user can decide.
sections.watch_out: The two area figures and the quoted source text are fixed in the code.

sections.name: CaseDashboardContent (part 11)
sections.title: Holder name difference card
sections.what: Shows the second difference card, comparing two spellings of the holder name, with a button to mark it reviewed.
sections.why: Lets the user decide whether two name spellings refer to the same person.
sections.watch_out: The two names are fixed demo names, so this card does not compare real records.

sections.name: CaseDashboardContent (part 12)
sections.title: Documents panel
sections.what: Shows a section with three document cards for the historical record, current record, and survey entry, each with a count of extracted items and a link to the documents page.
sections.why: Gives a single place to open the source documents.
sections.watch_out: The counts of 6, 5, and 4 are fixed and do not come from the documents.

sections.name: CaseDashboardContent (part 13)
sections.title: Document cards and reset button
sections.what: Finishes the three document cards and places the reset button below them.
sections.why: Groups the reset action with the documents area for demo use.
sections.watch_out: The reset action is visible on the dashboard, so it is easy to press by accident on a real case.

sections.name: CaseDashboardPage
sections.title: Detailed case explorer links
sections.what: Shows a grid of links to the detail pages, such as documents, verification, family tree, timeline, and next action, with labels in both languages.
sections.why: Lets the user reach each detail page from the dashboard.
sections.watch_out: Each link depends on the matching page existing under the case address.

summary: The main dashboard for a case. It shows a visual summary of differences between land records, but many numbers, names and labels are fixed demo text rather than values calculated from the case.
purpose: Gives the user one screen with progress, differences to review, document links, and links to the detail pages.
why: Reason not stated in the code. The fixed values suggest it is a visual prototype for a demo.
how: Keeps a record of which differences the user has reviewed in browser storage. Shows a progress count, two difference cards with review buttons, gauges, a map tile, document cards, a reset button, and a grid of links to detail pages. Short messages appear after actions.
inputs: Case details from the case wrapper, the chosen language, the saved review marks in browser storage, and user clicks.
outputs: The dashboard, short toast messages, updated review marks in browser storage, and a reset request to the server for demo cases.
risks: Fixed figures such as 15 percent, 1.02 acre, the holder name, and the document counts do not change with the real case. Users may read them as real results. The reset button calls a demo reset endpoint, and what it deletes is not visible in this file.
debug: If a number looks wrong, first check whether it is fixed text in this file. If review marks reset unexpectedly, check the browser storage entry named bs-reviewed. If the reset fails, check the reset endpoint response.
